recipes.name: Country Style Green Beans with Red Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 2 (14.5 ounce) cans green beans, drained and rinsed
10 small red potatoes, peeled and cubed

steps.text: Place turkey tails and onion in a 4-quart Dutch oven and fill half way with water. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat until meat falls off the bones, about 2 hours. Remove and discard bones and skin; return meat to the pot.
Add green beans to the Dutch oven and simmer for 20 minutes, then add the potatoes. Simmer until potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork, 10 to 15 minutes longer.

raw_recipe.headline: Country Style Green Beans with Red Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These green beans with smoked turkey and potatoes are a spectacular dish. The large quantity is great for special events or church dinners. The turkey tails make an excellent broth.

review.reviewBody: I give this recipe a five because I have grown up with something very similar to this one and have always loved it. Living in Kentucky for many years, I have eaten this hundreds of times except cooked with ham hocks. This time I didn't have any ham hocks (or other necks or parts on hand) and just added beef bullion instead to my water. It gives it a 'meaty' flavor without any meat or parts. I also add lots of chopped garlic (in place of powder) and several tsp. of Mrs. Dash salt-free seasoning. I also added a can of dark red kidney beans, drained and rinsed, to make a complete meatless main dish with lots of protein and fiber. I served it with some long grain and wild rice cooked with mushrooms, onion, and peas and called it a meal! You can play around with this recipe a lot. It's designed to be versatile, to fit many tastes.
This was delicious. I have no idea where one would get smoked turkey tails so I used smoked ham hock. Sped things up by using my Insta-Pot for the first step.

It turned out very delicious. I slow cooked smoked turkey necks in a crock pot for 6 hours. Removed them and pulled the meat from the neck and placed back in the crockpot. I then added canned green beans, potatoes, onions and a little chicken broth and cooked for about another hour. I did boil the potatoes in water and chicken broth to soften them before adding to the crock pot.

Delicious. Couple of amendments on my part though:
- whole garlic unpeeled in the broth instead of powder
- add the potatoes first, simmer for X minutes as written, THEN
- add the canned green beans because they're already cooked, simmer for X minutes further til potatoes cooked (pierce with a fork).

Smoked turkey tails hard to get here (never seen them) but this would work with any smoked meats e.g., ham hocks, smoked wings or drums, etc.

I thought this was a great recipe base, because I made a couple of changes. I left out the turkey meat. I already had meat as a main dish and wanted the Red Potatoes and Green Beans as a side dish . I boiled the red potatoes till almost done, while sauteing the onions in 3 Tbls. of Bacon grease. For about 5 mins. on a medium heat, then added the 2 cans (drained) of green beans. Then mixed well with onions and cooked about 5 mins. or so, then cut up red potatoes and added to green beans and onions mixed together seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic powder. My Husband loved the recipe. Thank you for sharing it with everyone. !!!
I've made this per the recipe as well as adding my own little flair. Used fresh green beans added before the potatoes, sauted fresh garlic with the onions before adding. Great both ways!

Who cooks canned green beans for 30 minutes? yuck. I hate the taste of canned anything anyway so I used fresh. I also was grossed out by "turkey tails " so I used wings. tasted delicious. Added a little butter and parsley at the end and it was so good.
It was great the only suggestion I make is that you only use one teaspoon of pepper not two that's way too much pepper

I have also served this recipe for years, except I use fresh or frozen green beans (2 bags) and 1 pound of skinless smoked sausage cut into coins. Add water or broth and put all ingredients in the pot at once and cook until the beans are tender. Try it sometime. It's less greasy than ham hocks, but oh so good! And even better warmed up the next day!

This recipe was great ! i used smoked turkey legs and simmered it in my crock pot overnight by morning i removed them from the broth and took all the bones and skin off put the meat back in the pot i added all other items and it was done by 12 GREAT!! i made enough for 12 people they all loved it! It was simple enough for me and im not a cook at all! thanks

Nothing says Sunday like these Green Beans & Potatoes. I didn't have any turkey tails (not even sure where to find them) or hamhocks, so I added country ham and skipped the first 2 hours of cooking. The country ham is quite salty though, so there was no need to add more salt. Also popped in the oven as suggested to crisp up the taters. Thanks.

I'm so glad to see this recipe. I've been making this forever and always used the turkey tail. This is the first time I've seen a recipe include turkey tails as a main ingredient. So much flavor. Thanks.

I followed the recipe and it came out good however, I am not a fan of black pepper. Too peppery..the next time I make it, I will cut back the pepper. I used turkey legs instead of turkey necks and it still gave the broth a good taste.
This dish was all the rave at my Thanksgiving dinner. My picky daughter love it. I will be making this dish on a weekly basis.
Great recipe! I tweaked it a little by adding a couple chicken bouillon cubes and I used a smoked turkey wing and Yukon gold potatoes. My family loves it!
I actually used fresh green beans. I thought that it would be better so everything was more firm then very soft. It was great.

I think it needed more seasoning. I tasted it as it cooked. And, I ended up adding more pepper, seasoning salt and a tad bit of cayenne pepper, for a smidgen of spiciness. We don't eat pork, and I didn't have any smoked turkey parts. So, I added some chicken bouillon cubes to the water. It tasted good. Also, I used fresh ingredients (potatoes, beans, garlic cloves, onion), since I'm trying to get away from cooking with jarred/canned/processed foods. Overall, it was a good recipe. I'm adding it to my repertoire and look forward to making it again.
In our house, we call these hillbilly green beans. Only we use vegetarian bakon bits to give it that smoky salty taste. It cooks down rapidly and the kids finish the entire pot they love it so much.
Excellent. I think next time I will make some cornbread and wild rice. Seems like a dish that would make a great side in the holidays. Thanks

i thinl this will be a great recipe but and more green beans and less of the turkey tails and if you want a meat use a chop steak marinaded in A1 sauce and cooked with the extra green beans and it is just fantastic! Love JERSEYsSHORE!
